title: RC Filters Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav turns up the bass knob on his speaker: the deep drums get louder, the high cymbals stay the same. How does a circuit pick out only the low notes? In this animated lesson a sieve shows the idea of a filter, and we see why a capacitor acts like a wall at low frequency and a shortcut at high frequency (X_C = 1/2πfC).

On a live breadboard a signal generator drives a low-pass RC filter (1.6 kΩ and 0.1 μF) while the oscilloscope shows the input and output at 100 Hz, 1 kHz and 10 kHz. Then we swap the parts to make a high-pass filter and the result flips. We treat each filter as a voltage divider, find the cut-off frequency f_c = 1/(2πRC) where the output is 70.7% of the input (half the power), draw the frequency response of both filters, and work an example (f_c ≈ 995 Hz). Then the exam trap (at cut-off the voltage is not half), where it is asked, an original board pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 37 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 5: Application of D.C and A.C to Passive Components (Karnataka I PUC Electronics).
